focus: περνάω 'pass' also means 'get accepted' – πέρασα στο πανεπιστήμιο = I got in; romanize the full quoted phrase, not just pérasa.
Past-tense μπόρεσα means 'managed to', not just 'was able' – a meaning shift English 'could' doesn't make; say it plainly instead of leaning on 'aorist'.
δασκάλα vs καθηγήτρια split by school level – real confusable pair, but καθηγήτρια is cited without romanization.
καθόλου stacks onto δεν and the double negative is standard Greek – keep the insight, romanize the whole δεν... καθόλου pattern.
σχολή (university department) vs σχολείο (kids' school) is a genuine landmine – but σχολείο is cited without romanization.
Greek has a VERB for being late – άργησα να = 'I was late to (do)', no adjective needed; drop the 'aorist of αργώ' framing.
Greek 'holds' notes where English 'takes' them – κρατάω σημειώσεις; the tip currently reads as a bare phrase gloss and misses the verb-choice contrast.
ιδιαίτερα normally means 'especially/particular' but κάνω ιδιαίτερα = give private lessons – surface the two-meanings surprise, not just the set-phrase gloss.
Masculine -ές nouns take the unexpected -δες plural (ο καφές → καφέδες) – a real inflection trap, but frame it as the pattern, not 'the plural of ο καφές'.
βάση ('base') also means the university admission cutoff in the Panellinies system – lead with the two-meanings hook rather than a context gloss.
αντιγράφω 'copy' IS the word for cheating on a test – good landmine, but αντιγραφή is cited without romanization.
δεν + τίποτα double negative is the normal way to say 'nothing' – keep the insight, romanize the whole δεν... τίποτα pattern.
παρέα ('company, friend group') used adverbially means 'together' – μελετάμε παρέα; currently a gloss with filler ('a very common everyday word').
όρεξη is literally 'appetite' and extends to any desire – δεν έχω όρεξη = I don't feel like it; lead with the literal-appetite hook.
κολλάω is literally 'to stick/glue' – a frozen video 'sticks'; surface the literal logic instead of a bare tech gloss.
κινητό (literally 'the mobile/movable one') is the everyday word for phone vs more formal τηλέφωνο – but τηλέφωνο is cited without romanization.
The απο- prefix reverses συνδέομαι 'connect' into 'disconnect/log out' – a reusable prefix pattern; συνδέομαι is cited without romanization.
ανεβάζω/κατεβάζω are literally 'take up'/'take down' = upload/download – nice mirror pair, but κατεβάζω is cited without romanization.
μου τελείωσαν = 'they ran out on me' – the data is the subject and you are the μου; the experiencer construction is the insight, not the δεδομένα gloss.
κλείνω 'close' is the verb for booking – κλείνω εισιτήρια/τραπέζι; surface the close-means-book surprise instead of a phrase gloss.
απαντάω takes σε – in Greek you answer TO the call (απαντάω στην κλήση); make the required preposition the point instead of a phrase gloss.
πιο + adjective forms the comparative with no ending change (ο πιο στενός = the closest) – solid insight, but the tip uses a banned em dash.
κάνω παρέα με = hang out with, literally 'make company' – keep the everyday idiom, fix the banned em dash.
λείπω reverses English 'miss': the missed person is the subject and the misser sits in σε (λείπεις στην παρέα = the group misses you) – fix the em dash and make the reversal explicit.
Past-tense γνώρισα of 'know' (γνωρίζω) means 'met for the first time' – the know-becomes-met shift is the insight; drop the 'aorist of' framing and the em dash.
ο ένας τον άλλον is the fixed reciprocal formula for 'one another' – keep, but fix the banned em dash.
The clitic της before the verb means 'to her' – you entrust something TO someone; της and the pattern words are cited without romanization.
κρατάω 'hold' also means 'last' for durations (η φιλία κρατάει είκοσι χρόνια) – fix the banned em dash.
από παιδιά is literally 'from kids' = since childhood – nice literal logic, fix the banned em dash.
χαίρομαι ends in -ομαι and looks passive but just means 'I'm glad' – keep that; cut the 'deponent' jargon and the paradigm listing.
περνάω ωραία is literally 'pass nicely' = have a good time – keep the literal-logic hook, fix the banned em dash.
